scope: All 8 proposed 1995 missions; no arbitrary enemy placement
provenance: Original J2ME 3.3.0 not yet traced; currently active placements are authored remake greybox only
principle: A guard exists because a post or duty exists, not because the designer needs an enemy at an arbitrary coordinate
rules: Each guard must have stable ID, mission/sector, duty, protected asset, work route or fixed observation post, shift/pause, patrol height, local stimulus semantics, alarm response and believable recovery.
No guard may appear inside a sealed cell, cross between floors without a navigable connector, detect through solid walls, or spawn as a scripted wave solely because an item was picked up.
Use authored patrol stops for inspecting doors, trucks, machinery or occupied cells; dwell/face/scan at the post without freezing on other decks.
Any extra guard requires a new documented job that fits architecture, plus valid connected floor/collision path and a source/canon grade.
After capture, alarm, prisoner rescue, gate opening or revisits, assigned posts may reconfigure; guards do not reset magical knowledge, teleport or repopulate unrelated rooms.
Guard absence is legitimate: empty corridors, downtime, and opportunities for observation form the pacing between real security stations.
Do not use randomized enemy counts or scattered spawn transforms as production placements; prototypes can use explicit authored contracts only.
Save/reload guard defeats, alarm knowledge and changed duties once the persistent security simulation is implemented; current runtime lacks full continuity.
Every combat guard must have readable detection, hearing, occlusion, route return and a readable attack wind-up; do not require all guards to be engaged.
Boss arenas have separate specialized duties (detention enforcer, anti-personnel fire, hostage exploitation) and must preserve source-like routes and alternative solutions.
